---
title: "Violent Crime"
toc: true
---

Violent crime involves the use or threat of physical force. It is best studied through individual propensity, situational triggers, social relations, and institutional response.

## A simple mechanism map
 
Violent crime can be understood as the joint product of individual predispositions, situational triggers, and social environments.
 
```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[Individual Factors] --> D[Violent Behaviour]
    B[Situational Triggers] --> D
    C[Social Environment] --> D
 
    A --> A1[Impulsivity]
    A --> A2[Self-control]
    A --> A3[Past Victimization]
 
    B --> B1[Conflict]
    B --> B2[Alcohol or Intoxication]
    B --> B3[Weapon Availability]
 
    C --> C1[Peer Effects]
    C --> C2[Local Norms]
    C --> C3[Low Trust and Weak Guardianship]
```

## Mechanisms to connect

- retaliation and status contests
- alcohol, impulsivity, and self-control
- peer effects and local norms
- perceived legitimacy of police and courts

## Models to try

- repeated conflict and retaliation games
- deterrence models with perceived sanction risk
- network diffusion of violence
